results.content: # The people of France are in an extraordinary funk about their future – here’s why. The race to succeed Emmanuel Macron is looming, but rarely has the mood been so gloomy or the lure of extremist solutions so alarming. As the campaign for next year’s presidential election hits its stride with ever more wannabes declaring their candidacies, the country is in a particularly sullen mood. In spring 2011, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, the then head of the IMF and an admired former finance minister, was hot favourite to become the Socialist party candidate who would beat the incumbent conservative Nicolas Sarkozy in the 2012 race. results.content: # Americans’ satisfaction with schools is at a low point, new Gallup poll shows. * Americans’ satisfaction with K-12 education has dropped to 32%, the lowest in nearly three decades, a Gallup poll shows. Americans’ satisfaction with the quality of K-12 education in the country has hit a low point, driven by a growing political divide and concerns that schools are not preparing children for college and future jobs. results.content: # California voters deeply frustrated by length of November ballot, state and nation’s direction. * Californians are deeply pessimistic about the direction of the state and nation, expecting tough economic times and are sour on both major political parties, according to a new poll. * Likely voters are split over a one-time wealth tax on billionaires and rival measures that could nullify it, while saying they oppose a voter ID proposal and support Democrat Xavier Becerra for governor.
